request: Analyze GSE233004 for PMID 38686869 (Moderate Endurance Exercise Increases Arrhythmia Susceptibility and Modulates Cardiac Structure and Function in a Sexually Dimorphic Manner.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.sample_inclusion: 3 sedentary + 3 exercised LV per sex, n=12 (S1.7.p1, FIG6 legend)
final.primary_estimand: Effect of 6-week moderate treadmill endurance exercise on LV gene expression, estimated separately within each sex (exercised vs sedentary)
planned_contrasts: Female EX vs Female Sed (FIG6B/C; S2.5.p2: 1 DEG, Ddx3y up in EX)
Male EX vs Male Sed (FIG6B/D; S2.5.p2: 22 DEGs)
Female vs Male within Sed (FIG7; 896 DEGs) and within EX (174 DEGs) -- sex comparisons, not exercise estimands
final.repeated_measure_unit: none for RNA-seq (one heart per mouse)
final.paper_method: DESeq2 Wald test, BH-adjusted p (S1.8.p3), per-sex exercised vs sedentary comparison

paper_threshold.source_locator: S1.8.p3 (Padj < 0.05; log2FC cutoff 0 for volcano/KEGG; 2 only for top-gene plots); FIG6 legend

final.paper_direction_convention: log2FC = Sedentary minus Exercised (S1.7.p1); positive = up in Sed. Our tables use EX vs SED (positive = up in EX).

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: Methods S1.7.p1 and S1.8.p3 define DESeq2 Wald + BH, padj<0.05; the DEG counts quoted in S2.5.p2 come from the volcano plots, whose log2FC cutoff is 0 (S1.8.p3). The exercise question is answered per sex in Figure 6; Figure 7 is sex-difference, not exercise.

checks: GEO: Mus musculus heart, bulk tissue, WT, Exercise/Sedentary, treadmill 1 km/h 45 min/day 5 d/wk 6 wk
12 samples = 3 per sex x treatment, matching S1.7.p1

ownership.reasoning: Paper S1.p1 cites GSE233004; series design and n match the methods.

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns (FEX360...) equal metadata title exactly for 12/12. Sex and treatment are encoded in the title prefix and agree with the 'description' and 'treatment' characteristics.

matrix.reasoning: All values integer, 0..3.1e6, library sizes 22-33M; GEO data_processing: STAR + featureCounts hit counts (gene_id). The paper's input to DESeq2 is the same counts.

candidates.value: pooled EX vs SED across sexes
candidates.reason_rejected: paper reports exercise effects per sex (FIG6); pooled additive model kept only as exploratory

candidates.value: Female vs Male within each treatment (FIG7)
candidates.reason_rejected: sex-difference contrast, not an exercise estimand; outside the request

design.reasoning: Paper FIG6 compares exercised with sedentary mice of each sex separately (n=3 vs 3). Separate per-sex fits match 'determined for each group' (S1.7.p1). n=3 per arm meets the minimum.

covariates.name: sex
covariates.disposition: stratified (separate fits per sex); used as an additive covariate only in the exploratory pooled model

covariance.reasoning: Independent animals, one LV each; no batch, lane or date recorded in GEO or the paper. Sex is balanced with treatment (3/3 in each sex), so it is not confounded.

deviations: pydeseq2 rather than R DESeq2; independent filtering/Cook's outlier handling may differ slightly
paper does not state whether the per-sex comparisons used separate fits or one model with a 4-level group; separate fits chosen

method.reasoning: Raw featureCounts counts support the paper's DESeq2 route directly.

threshold.reasoning: S1.8.p3: Padj < 0.05, log2FC cutoff 0 for volcano/KEGG (the DEG counts). The |log2FC| > 2 rule applied only to the top-gene panels and is kept as a labelled audit rule.

caveats: Paper's log2FC sign is Sed minus EX; ours is EX minus Sed.

Ddx3y (Y-linked) reported up in exercised females; female samples carry low Ddx3y counts (FEX 14-26 vs FSE 0-5) while Xist is uniformly high in females, so this looks like low-level male-read contamination or cross-mapping, not a sex mislabel.

study.reasoning: Counts and named genes from S2.5.p2 and FIG6.

discrepancies.data: our tables report EX vs SED

discrepancies.paper: only DEG in females, up in EX; attributed to probe cross-reactivity (S2.5.p2)
discrepancies.data: female Ddx3y counts 14-26 (EX) vs 0-5 (SED); males ~1700-2300; Xist high only in females

executions.name: trt_EX_vs_SED_sex-F
executions.reasoning: FIG6 female exercised vs sedentary, DESeq2 Wald, separate fit

executions.name: trt_EX_vs_SED_sex-M
executions.reasoning: FIG6 male exercised vs sedentary, DESeq2 Wald, separate fit

executions.name: joint4
executions.reasoning: Alternative reading of the paper's DESeq2 setup: one model on all 12 samples with a 4-level sex x treatment group (~ cell), per-sex EX vs SED contrasts extracted from it with pooled dispersion. Separate per-sex fits gave 24 (F) / 0 (M) DEGs vs the paper's 1 / 22.

executions.reasoning: Not in the paper: pooled exercise main effect adjusted for sex (~ sex + trt), all 12 samples

enrichment.reasoning: paper reports KEGG pathways per sex (FIG6E/F)
paper reports KEGG pathways per sex (FIG6E/F); oxidative phosphorylation enriched
